newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich wants Democrats to list foreign donors.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich wants Democrats to list foreign donors.

text.p: Republican House Speaker Newt Gingrich on Monday called on the Democratic Party to release a full list of foreign contributors following reports the party accepted a large contribution from an Indonesian couple.
"The Democratic National Committee should release a list of all the non-Americans they've gotten money from," Gingrich told reporters before addressing a Republican fund raising dinner.

With Republican candidate Bob Dole running behind President Bill Clinton in the polls, Republicans have seized on the $425,000 contribution made to the Democratic Party by an Indonesian couple who were living in the United States.
"There's no question this is a very severe issue -- not of ethics, of law breaking," Gingrich said.
It is illegal for foreigners to contribute to U.S. political candidates or parties but aliens living in the United States can legally contribute.
Gingrich said more needed to be known about the Indonesian couple and whether the contribution represented "money laundering."

Republicans suspect the contribution may be linked to an Indonesian financial conglomerate, the Lippo Group. They believe Indonesian James Riady, who has ties to Clinton, may have used his influence in getting the contribution made.
Attention has focused particularly on John Huang, a former vice chairman of Lippo's California banking subsidiary who moved on to become vice finance chairman of the Democratic National Committee.
Gingrich and Republican National Committee Chairman Haley Barbour said their party did not accept such contributions.
Gingrich himself is the subject of a probe by the House of Representatives ethics committee on charges he improperly used tax-exempt funds for political purposes.
Clinton's spokesman Mike McCurry called the charges over the contribution desperation politics.
